page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal server configured with 288 vCPUs and 2232.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The system is powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, featuring 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by a 504 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations. Specifically, it achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, passmark CPU physics, and redis SET operations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching top-tier performance in both small-block cached and large-block uncached read and write operations. However, single-core CPU performance and small-model LLM text generation speeds are lower, with the latter falling into the bottom tier.

Given its bare-metal architecture, high memory density, and dedicated compute resources, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise workloads that require massive memory capacity without GPU acceleration. It is suited for high-throughput database operations, memory-intensive data processing, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server featuring 288 dedicated vCPUs and 2232.0 GB of DDR5 RAM. Powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at 4.2 GHz, it delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth. The server includes 144 physical cores, a 504 MB L3 cache, and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX, though it lacks local storage and GPUs. Benchmark data highlights its exceptional capabilities in database operations, redis SET operations, and multi-threaded decompression, while single-core performance remains average. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, large-scale database management, and high-throughput data processing.
